newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia by-election hangs on minor parties.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia by-election hangs on minor parties.

text.p: Anti-immigration and pro-shooter votes could determine the outcome of Australia's Lindsay by-election in New South Wales on Saturday, with polls showing a narrow gap between the major parties.
Liberal candidate Jackie Kelly was ahead on primary votes with 46 percent compared with Labor candidate Ross Free's 41.5 percent in the Morgan poll published in the October 15 Bulletin magazine.
But after the distribution of preference votes the telephone survey of 977 electors taken in early October found Kelly would only inch ahead with 51 percent compared with Free's 49 percent.
The poll found the votes of eight percent of the undecided electors could be crucial to the preferential vote outcome.
Both Free and Kelly have been vying for preference votes from the minor shooters party and anti-immigration party.
Labor only needs about 1,300 votes to inch ahead of Liberal which holds the seat with a narrow 1.6 percent margin.
Under Australia's complicated preferential voting system votes for minor candidates are redistributed to candidates with larger numbers of votes according to preferences marked by voters.
This continues until one candidate scores a clear majority.

The Lindsay by-election, the first since the government won office on March 2, was ordered by the High Court when it found Jackie Kelly contravened the constitution by working for the government as an airforce member and holding dual Australia-New Zealand citizenship.
